content: The text provided appears to be a list of references from various studies, articles, and reports related to pharmaceutical pricing, policies, and healthcare systems. Each entry includes the title, authors, publication details, and a note indicating that the study design was deemed ineligible for a specific purpose. 1. The study by Dusetzina SB, Conti RM, Yu NL, and Bach PB, published in JAMA Internal Medicine in 2017, examined the association between prescription drug price rebates in Medicare Part D and their impact on patient out-of-pocket costs and federal spending. However, the study design was deemed ineligible. 2. Dutta A and Bandyopadhyay S explored the effectiveness of policy interventions aimed at improving access to medicines for both poor and non-poor populations. This study, published in the International Journal of Health Planning and Management in 2019, was also found to have an ineligible study design. 3. The study design was considered ineligible. 4. This research, published in Pharmacoeconomics in 2014, was also deemed ineligible due to its study design. 5.
